mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% over three months signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreased by more than 0.5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a single month signals a strengthening demand for housing, which boosts the construction sector and related industries, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a single month signals a weakening supply side, which may indicate a slowing economy and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures over three months signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods with sustained RSAFS increases.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in GDP by more than 1% in a quarter signals a weakening economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 decreased by more than 1% in a quarter.
